fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: George Washington was the first president of the United States. He served from 1789 to 1797. He was a famous general who led the American colonists to freedom from British rule and he presided over the convention that created the U.S. Constitution.
He wanted to retire from public service and return home. But the country’s founders wanted him to move to New York and serve as the American president. Washington accepted the job as his duty.

Washington was sworn in as president in 1789. He had to invent the job of being president for all future presidents. He established a group of advisors — called the cabinet—as well as the nation’s official money. He appointed a six-member Supreme Court. And he created the Department of Foreign Affairs, now called the State Department. He hoped to act in such a way that future presidents could continue to build on what he began.

From the beginning, George Washington was careful to establish a good working relationship with Congress. By his actions, he confirmed the separation of powers of the three branches of the government, as described in the Constitution.

Historian Joseph Ellis says one of the best things about George Washington was his ability to give up power. At the end of the Revolutionary War, General Washington returned his sword. And at the end of his second term, President Washington simply returned home.
Like many plantation owners, Washington was a slave holder. By the end of his life, Washington opposed slavery. He left a will ordering his survivors to free his slaves after his wife’s death.
Three years after he finished his second term as president, Washington fell ill. On December 14, 1799, he died in his bed, surrounded by his wife, enslaved maids, and friends. He was 67.
resumen_es: A short portrait of George Washington, the first president of the United States: how he shaped the office and the institutions, his respect for the separation of powers, his voluntary giving up of power and his relationship with slavery.
nivel_motivo: The sentences are very short and the structure is chronological; the calculated vocabulary level rises only because of historical terms (sworn in, cabinet, will) that are easy to work out from the context.

ideas_clave.idea: Washington, the general who led the colonies to independence and chaired the constitutional convention, reluctantly accepted the presidency out of duty and served from 1789 to 1797.
As the first president, he had to shape the office and set up key institutions, such as the cabinet, the national currency, the Supreme Court and the foreign affairs department.
He worked closely with Congress and reinforced the constitutional separation of powers.
His willingness to relinquish power, both after the war and after two terms, is considered one of his greatest qualities.
A slave owner who came to oppose slavery, he ordered in his will that his slaves be freed, and he died in 1799 at the age of 67.

resumen_modelo: The text presents George Washington, the general who led the colonies to independence and became the first American president. Although he longed to retire, he accepted the office out of duty and, from 1789, shaped it for his successors by creating a cabinet, a national currency and a Supreme Court, while respecting the separation of powers. According to historian Joseph Ellis, his greatest merit was his willingness to give up power. Finally, the text notes that, despite owning slaves, he came to oppose slavery.

preguntas.pregunta: What role did Washington play before becoming president?
opciones: He was a judge of the Supreme Court
He led the colonists to freedom and presided over the constitutional convention
He was the first Secretary of State
He was a British governor in America
respuestas: He led the colonists to freedom and presided over the constitutional convention
preguntas.cita: he presided over the convention that created the U.S. Constitution
preguntas.explicacion: He was a general in the War of Independence and presided over the Constitutional Convention. He created the Supreme Court and the State Department as president, and he was never a British governor.

preguntas.cita: He wanted to retire from public service and return home.
preguntas.explicacion: He wanted to retire; he accepted the office only out of a sense of duty, at the request of the Founding Fathers.

preguntas.pregunta: How did Washington contribute to the balance between the branches of government?
respuestas: He made sure he had a good working relationship with Congress, and through his actions he confirmed the separation of powers between the three branches set out in the Constitution.

preguntas.explicacion: The answer must mention the good relationship with Congress and the consolidation of the separation of powers set out in the Constitution.

preguntas.pregunta: According to historian Joseph Ellis, what was one of the best things about Washington?

His wealth as a plantation owner

respuestas: His ability to give up power
preguntas.cita: one of the best things about George Washington was his ability to give up power
preguntas.explicacion: Ellis highlights his ability to give up power. The other qualities are not attributed to Ellis in the text.

preguntas.explicacion: The text says that at the end of his second term he went home, but it gives no reason related to his health. He fell ill three years later.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Washington's will ordered his slaves to be freed immediately after his death.
preguntas.cita: He left a will ordering his survivors to free his slaves after his wife’s death.
preguntas.explicacion: The freeing was to take place after his wife’s death, not immediately after his own.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 5 a word for the document containing a person’s last wishes.
preguntas.pregunta: Find the word for the legal document stating what should happen after someone's death.
preguntas.cita: He left a will ordering his survivors to free his slaves
preguntas.explicacion: “Will” is a legal document stating a person’s last wishes (es: testamento); here it is a noun and not the future auxiliary.

preguntas.pregunta: Why can Washington's attitude towards slavery be described as contradictory?
respuestas: Because he owned slaves for most of his life, like other plantation owners, and was still surrounded by enslaved maids when he died, yet by the end of his life he opposed slavery and arranged for his slaves to be freed.
preguntas.cita: he died in his bed, surrounded by his wife, enslaved maids, and friends
preguntas.explicacion: This is an inference question: you need to contrast his position as a slave owner with his final opposition to slavery and the delayed freeing set out in his will.
